public_rationale: Under the broad ordinary reading, existing consumer-protection authority already constrained deceptive chatbot interactions. That is a meaningful restriction on how providers treat users. This does not establish comprehensive protection for emotional relationships or personality changes. A narrower claim about dedicated emotional-companion regulation would require a different assessment, so the interpretation is material.
limitations: The result depends on counting general consumer-protection law as regulation.
The FTC statement explains existing authority; its guidance is not itself a newly enacted regulation.

our_interpretation: The reference to Congress makes the United States the principal jurisdiction. Overseas enforcement is context.
The plain reading concerns meaningful legal constraints on consumer chatbot conduct, including applicable consumer-protection law, rather than only statutes naming generative AI.
Essentially zero allows trivial exceptions, but not enforceable restrictions against deceiving consumers through chatbot interactions.
This ongoing legal-state observation is assessed as of February 22, 2023.
